newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Caltex to increase investment, oil output in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Caltex to increase investment, oil output in 1997.

text.p: PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia said on Friday it would increase oil investment spending to $400 million in 1997 from $344 million in 1996 and projected oil production would rise to 785,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 758,000 bpd.
"We will boost investment to $400 million in 1997 from $344 million in 1996, mainly for exploration and exploitation," Caltex President Baihaki Hakim told Reuters in an interview.
"We will increase production to around 785,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil in 1997 from 758,000 bpd in 1996," he said.
He said the Minas and Duri fields were still the backbone of Caltex oil production.
He said Minas currently produced 225,000 bpd and the Duri output was 275,000 bpd.

He said Caltex, a 50-50 venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, had received a financial incentive from Indonesian's state oil company Pertamina to further develop the Minas field through a steamflooding project.

"Pertamina has agreed to our proposal for a financial incentive to develop the Minas light oil steamflooding project to recover around 300 million to 400 million barrel of Minas crude reserves," Hakim said.
"This project is very risky and needs a high investment of around $630 million in total.

"The incentive is in the form of interest recovery for the Minas light oil steamflooding project. This is a case-by-case incentive where we are allowed to charge the interest as an operating cost. The current rule is we cannot charge (to Pertamina) the interest on loans," Hakim said.
